prompt: Sort a leaderboard of {playerId, score} arrays by score descending, breaking ties with the smaller playerId first, using a Comparator. Complete the rank method, then run the tests.
explanation: int[] has no natural order, so sorting it always needs an external Comparator. Comparator.comparingInt extracts the sort key, reversed() flips it for descending order, and thenComparingInt adds the ascending tiebreaker. Note that reversed() must be applied before the tiebreaker is chained, otherwise the tiebreaker would be reversed too.
hints: Start with java.util.Comparator.comparingInt((int[] row) -> row[1]) to compare by score.
Call .reversed() on that comparator to get descending scores, then chain .thenComparingInt(row -> row[0]) for the id tiebreak.
Pass the finished comparator to scores.sort(...) -- the list is sorted in place, so rank returns nothing.
